title: Passing an array and its length
goal: Pass an array and its active element count to a function. Explain why the same buffer can give different results with different lengths.

prerequisites.text: Check an index before reading an array element and trace the iterations of a loop.

terms.title: Capacity
terms.definition: The number of elements allocated in the array.

terms.title: Active length
terms.definition: The count of initial elements the function must process. It can be zero.

terms.title: Array parameter
terms.definition: A declaration such as const int values[] in a function parameter list. C adjusts it to a const int * parameter.

sections.title: One buffer can hold different numbers of active readings
paragraphs: Three cards on a table show 5, 8 and 2. In one call all three readings should be added. In another, the meter has supplied no active readings yet. The readings array still has three slots in both cases. Passing an active length of zero tells the function to skip all of them.
The contract has two parts. Pass the array’s starting address and the active length. The caller checks that the length is from 0 through capacity. The loop then reads only indices below length.

In main, readings names the array. The parameter declaration const int values[] becomes const int * inside sum. There, sizeof values gives the size of a pointer. The active element count comes from length.

sections.title: Sum three readings, then zero
paragraphs: The first call to sum passes an active length of 3. Here it equals the capacity. The second passes the same array and an active length of 0. Trace the changes in total and count the array reads.
steps: After reading indices 0, 1 and 2, the totals are 5, 13 and 15.
Second call. With length = 0, the first condition is false. The function returns the starting value 0.

sections.title: The result reveals where the loop stopped
paragraphs: A loop with index < length − 1 skips the last active position. Summing exposes that mistake when the last value is nonzero. For a threshold count, choose a case where the last element meets the threshold.
The compiler example declares two parameters for first_or_zero. The call supplies one argument. Locate the missing length in the declaration and explain where the program can compute it.

sections.title: Choose a test using only part of the array
paragraphs: For readings 2, 7 and 9 with threshold 7, predict the number of matches at lengths 3, 2 and 0. Only the full traversal includes the last value, 9. Trace how the length changes what the function does with the same array.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Check array-to-pointer conversion, the sizeof exception and array parameter adjustment.

selfcheck.prompt: What does sum(readings, 0) return in the example?
feedback: The first loop condition is false. The initial total is returned.
A sum of 5 requires reading the first element.
The sum is 15 when all three elements are processed.

selfcheck.prompt: What does sizeof values give inside sum with a const int values[] parameter?
options: The active length supplied by the caller
feedback: Compute capacity while the array type is available.
C adjusted the parameter type to a pointer.
The active length is passed separately in length.

selfcheck.prompt: The array has four slots and the function receives length = 2. Which indices may this call read, and what must the caller check first?
selfcheck.feedback: This call reads only indices 0 and 1. The caller checks 0 ≤ length ≤ capacity. When length is 2, the body of a loop using index < length runs twice.

stderrIncludes: too few arguments to function call

practice.title: Active readings at or above a threshold
practice.task: The readings array contains 5, 8, 2 and 8. The first input line gives an active length from 0 to 4 inclusive. The second gives a threshold from −99 to 99. Count how many of the first length values are at least the threshold. Print the count on one line. Print invalid for a missing line, malformed integer or out-of-range value. The supplied read_integer function handles the first two lines. Further input is ignored. Fix the loop limit in count_at_least.
practice.hint: Compare the last index visited by the starter with the final index in the active range. The range depends on length.
criteria: Inputs 4 and 8 should give 2, 2 and 8 should give 1, and 0 and 8 should give 0. Enter each pair on separate lines.
The function reads only the active range and counts values equal to the threshold.
A length above capacity or below zero is rejected before the call to count_at_least.

steps.action: Open Practice and check that 4 and 8 are on separate input lines. Select Run my code.
steps.why: Look for the match at the last value, 8.
steps.expected: The starter prints 1. With all four readings active, the required count is 2.

steps.action: Fix the loop bound in count_at_least and run again. Then change the first line to 2 and then to 0.
steps.why: The length sets the active range. At zero, the loop never starts.
steps.expected: The three runs at lengths 4, 2 and 0 give 2, 1 and 0 with threshold 8.

steps.action: Try length 5 with threshold 8. Keep main’s input check before the function call.
steps.why: A length greater than capacity violates the contract.
steps.expected: The output is invalid. The counting function is never called.

exercises.title: Independent transfer
exercises.task: Save your code to a local text file. In the lesson editor, replace readings with 6, 4, 6, 9 and 6. Keep threshold 6 and try the full length 5, the prefix of length 2, and length 0. Restore your saved code afterwards.
criteria: At the same threshold, the outputs are 4, 1 and 0 respectively.
Capacity comes from the declared array. The loop uses length.
